title: Inspect this page: Bytes & Bolts repairs
brief:
A phone repair shop near the campus has a dark-mode website. Dark mode is fine, but it has to be done with care. Five things on this page make it hard for some people to use: two you know well, three are new, and one of them is inside a table. Find them. Tick each one you find and write one sentence saying why it matters for a real user. Two items in the list are not true on this page.

To look at the real HTML: right-click anything on the sample page and choose Inspect. The browser's developer tools open and show the tag under your mouse.

vocabulary.gloss: a <th> cell: the name of a column or row, which a screen reader reads together with each data cell
a small picture used instead of a word, like a phone symbol for "call us"
an attribute that gives an element a name for screen readers when it has no visible text
a design with a dark background and light text; the contrast rules are the same

problems.label: A heading jumps from h1 straight to h4
problems.why: Screen readers and outlines use heading levels like a contents page; a skipped level makes the structure confusing.

problems.label: The price table has no header cells (th)
problems.why: A screen reader reads a cell together with its column header, so without th the listener hears "£35" and does not know what it is the price of.

problems.label: Dark grey text on the black background is hard to read
problems.why: Low contrast is tiring for everyone and unreadable for many people with low vision; dark mode still needs light text.

problems.label: A button is made from a <div>, not a <button>
problems.why: A div cannot be reached with the Tab key or pressed with Enter, so keyboard and screen-reader users cannot use it.

problems.label: The phone link in the header is only an icon, with no text
problems.why: A screen reader announces "link" and nothing else; a short text or an aria-label would say "call us".

problems.label: An image has no alt text
A form input has no label

hints: Start at the top of the page: right-click the green phone icon and choose Inspect. What text is inside the … ? Then read the headings in order.
Right-click a price in the table and Inspect: are the cells in the first row <th> or <td>? Then do the same for the green "Book a repair" button.
One paragraph is much harder to read than the rest: look under the button. Real problems: 5; the image and the form on this page are fine.
